summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease, type 1 diabetes, and a mechanical heart valve was admitted for evaluation and treatment of a non-healing left foot ulcer with dry gangrene. She underwent a diagnostic left lower extremity angiogram, which revealed a near-occlusive lesion in the left superficial femoral artery. She remained hemodynamically stable throughout her stay, with no complications from the procedure. IV vancomycin was continued for infection prophylaxis, and anticoagulation was managed with a heparin drip that was discontinued once her INR reached a therapeutic level of 3.1. She was discharged home with instructions to continue oral medications, receive IV vancomycin on dialysis days, and follow up for a scheduled left femoral endarterectomy. The patient tolerated a regular diet, ambulated independently, and had stable vital signs at discharge.
problems: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of the extremities with gangrene
